Wait, but when the diamond was at center (30,39), the white was at (30,39) = center. Hmm, unless the white marker is at the top vertex and the diamond's center was at (42,39)?? No — earlier I calculated the diamond's center as (30,39) from the bbox (18,27)-(42,51).
Wait, actually — maybe the white marker is at the top vertex of the diamond, and the diamond's center was at (30,39)... top vertex (18,39). White was at (30,39). Not the vertex.
OK, another thought: maybe the white marker is at the top vertex of the diamond, and the diamond's center was at (42,39)?? But the bbox said (18,27)-(42,51), center (30,39).
Whatever the marker semantics are, the diamond's center is now at (12,39). The diamond's top vertex is at row 0 = the board's edge. Can the diamond move any higher? The center is at row 12, and the vertex is at row 0. To hide the red dot, the center needs to be at (12,21): row 12 ✓ already achieved! Only 18 LEFTs are needed.
The diamond's center is already at row 12. So now just 18 LEFTs.

So: 18 LEFTs. The diamond's left vertex is currently at (12,27); after 18 LEFTs the center is at (12,21), left vertex at (12,9) — on-screen ✓.
